title: Tool isolation sandbox handshake probe
body:
Purpose
---
Personal scratchpad for an inbound/outbound handshake protocol between the runtime and sandboxed tool workers (local or remote). Goal: minimal trust surface, clear lifecycle for ephemeral tokens, and easy fallback for tool unavailability. This is deliberately informal — experiments and questions are inline.

Goals and constraints
- Fast start: worker can be spun up and start handling calls within 50–200ms of admission (warm path).
- Least privilege: tool worker receives only the minimum capabilities and data required per-call.
- Observable: handshake events must emit structured telemetry for SRE/Trace linking.
- Recoverable: runtime must be able to revoke and re-issue credentials without leaking session state.

Actors
- Runtime (R): Redwood process that orchestrates tool calls and enforces policy.
- Sandbox Worker (W): isolated process/container that executes the tool contract. Could be local process, sidecar, or remote ephemeral runner.
- Key Broker (K): KMS/KMS-proxy service used only for sealing short-lived keys (optional).

High-level flow (happy path)
1) R decides to open session for tool T (policy check + input memoization lookup).
2) R allocates ephemeral session id sid = r-uuid().
3) R requests a short-lived capability from Key Broker (or signs locally) to create token tok, TTL 60s. Token binds: {sid, tool-id, allowed-ops, nonce}.
4) R launches W (or selects existing warm W) and performs network handshake: Connect -> HELLO(sid, proto-version) -> W responds HELLO_ACK(challenge) -> R signs challenge -> W verifies -> transport moves to AUTH_READY.
5) R sends AUTH_GRANT(token, policy-hash, telemetry-tags).
6) W confirms ACCEPT and emits READY event.
7) Calls are performed: CALL(req-id, op, input_refs). Each call scoped to sid and per-call auth wrapper (call-token derived from tok + req-id).
8) On close or TTL lapse, R sends REVOKE(sid) and W acknowledges; W must purge in-memory keys and optionally call a sealed-storage wipe.

Core message shapes (sketch)
- HELLO: {"type":"HELLO","sid":"...","proto":"v1","capabilities": ["json-io","file-ref"]}
- HELLO_ACK: {"type":"HELLO_ACK","challenge":"base64"}
- AUTH_GRANT: {"type":"AUTH_GRANT","token":"jwt-like-b64","policy_hash":"sha256:...","telemetry": {"trace_id":"..."}}
- ACCEPT: {"type":"ACCEPT","worker_version":"0.3.1","warm":true}
- CALL: {"type":"CALL","req_id":"...","op":"tool.run","args_ref":"ref://...","deadline":"2024-11-20T12:00:00Z"}
- RESULT: {"type":"RESULT","req_id":"...","status":"ok|error","out_ref":"ref://...","profile": {"duration_ms": 42}}
- REVOKE: {"type":"REVOKE","sid":"...","reason":"policy_update"}

Security model notes
- Token binding: tokens are audience bound to a worker attestation (challenge) so stealing tok alone is insufficient. The challenge-response ties token to the worker's ephemeral key.
- Minimal token lifetime: default 60s for startup; tokens are renewed per-call if long sessions needed (renew window 40s).
- Call-level least privilege: create call-tokens via HMAC(token, req_id || op) so worker cannot reuse call token for different ops.
- Audit hooks: every AUTH_GRANT/REVOKE/CALL/RESULT must include trace_id and optional auth_principal for downstream auditing.

Attestation options (tradeoffs)
- Bare TLS client certs (local sidecars): simple, low ops, but weaker isolation.
- mTLS + SPIFFE identities: good if sidecars are managed and we have a mesh; heavier setup for local dev.
- WebAuthn-like challenge with ephemeral key (in-process): flexible, works with remote runners, but requires KMS for signing or an in-memory key manager.

Sequence diagram (ASCII)
R                        W                       K
| HELLO(sid)             |                       |
|----------------------->|                       |
|                       HELLO_ACK(ch)           |
|<-----------------------|                       |
| sign(ch) -> SIGNED      |                       |
|----------------------->|                       |
|                       VERIFY_SIGN             |
|                       ----------------------->|
|                       <--OK                   |
| AUTH_GRANT(token)      |                       |
|----------------------->|                       |
|                       ACCEPT -> READY         |
|<-----------------------|                       |
| CALL(req)              |                       |
|----------------------->|                       |
|                       RESULT(req)             |
|<-----------------------|                       |
| REVOKE(sid)            |                       |
|----------------------->|                       |
|                       ACK_REVOKE              |
|<-----------------------|                       |

Config sketch (runtime)
- sandbox:
  - max_workers_per_tool: 3
  - token_ttl_seconds: 60
  - renew_window_seconds: 40
  - attestation: "ephemeral-signature"
  - telemetry_emit: ["auth_grant","call_start","call_end","revoke"]

Open questions / TODOs
- Where to persist evidence of revocation for workers that are unreachable? (short answer: central revocation log + heartbeat-driven wipe)
- How to support long-running interactive tools that intentionally exceed token TTL? Options: refresh flow with refresh-token minted only when worker proves liveness. Need to specify refresh ACLs.
- Workbench: create a small harness that can emulate a misbehaving worker (replay attacks, delayed ACKs) and see runtime reaction under load.
- Integration with KMS: optional path vs default "local signing"; define threat model for both.

Experiments to run
- Warm vs cold start: measure 50th/95th/99th percentiles when launching local process vs reusing warm sidecar.
- Token compromise simulation: attempt to replay token on different process without challenge -> ensure rejection.
- Telemetry correlation: ensure each event has trace_id and that trace spans link to request and worker lifecycle.

Examples (toy data)
HELLO -> {"type":"HELLO","sid":"sid-7c6a","proto":"v1","capabilities":["json-io"]}
HELLO_ACK -> {"type":"HELLO_ACK","challenge":"b64=="}
AUTH_GRANT -> {"type":"AUTH_GRANT","token":"eyj...","policy_hash":"sha256:aa...","telemetry":{"trace_id":"t-123"}}

Notes to self
- Keep the initial protocol v1 intentionally small: focus on auth binding and observability. Add features (streaming IO, file mounts) as v1.x.
- Share this with Ethan for threat-model input and Nina for console/trace UX hooks.

End of scratchpad.
